column2: '1278445758']	Jamie Dimon taps Jeff Bezos
column4: and Jim Farley for $1.5T national-security initiative	"Jamie Dimon’s JPMorgan Chase just unveiled a list of business leaders and retired government officials that will make up a new advisory team to guide the investment bank’s $1.5 trillion national security initiative.

column1: The external advisory council
column2: announced on Monday
column3: features prominent tech business leaders Jeff Bezos and Michael Dell as well as Ford CEO Jim Farley
column4: alongside a number of national security and defense experts.

column1: JPMorgan Chase announced its national security push—coined the Security and Resilience Initiative (SRI)—in October by saying it would first invest up to $10 billion in direct equity and venture capital to companies it characterizes as paramount to U.S. national security.
Dimon also said on Monday he poached one of Warren Buffett’s personally selected investors to head the investment fund starting in January.
Both of the announcements are initial steps to realizing the company’s national security pledge
column2: which will span the next 10 years.

column1: The council will be chaired by Dimon himself
column2: and will “convene periodically” to “help spur growth and innovation in industries critical to the United States’ national security and economic resiliency
column3: ” the company said in its press release.

column1: “We are humbled by the extraordinary group of leaders and public servants who have agreed to join our efforts as senior advisors to the SRI
column2: ” Dimon said in the Monday announcement. “With their help
column3: we can ensure that our firm takes a holistic approach to addressing key issues facing the United States—supporting companies across all sizes and development stages through advice

column1: Here is a list of the advisory council members:
Business leaders
Jeff Bezos
column2: executive chairman and founder of Amazon and founder of Blue Origin

column1: Bezos previously partnered with Dimon and Warren Buffett on the not-for-profit Haven health care venture in 2018
column2: which was backed by Amazon
column4: and Berkshire Hathaway. Dimon has said the two “hit it off” in 1999
column5: and Bezos even discussed hiring Dimon as Amazon’s president before Dimon chose to stay in banking.

column1: Michael Dell
column2: CEO of Dell Technologies

column1: Dell worked closely with Dimon and JPMorgan when the bank led the multibillion‑dollar financing for Dell’s $67 billion takeover of tech giant EMC in 2015
column2: at the time the largest tech deal ever.

column1: Jim Farley
column2: CEO of Ford Motor Company

column1: Farley has publicly warned about U.S. dependence on China for chips and rare earths
column2: arguing it is a strategic vulnerability. In a third-quarter earnings call in October
column3: he told investors he had discussed these issues with U.S. officials as a chip shortage caused by China threatened to impact the automaker.

column1: Alex Gorsky
column2: former CEO of Johnson & Johnson

column1: Gorsky
column2: most recently the company’s former executive chairman
column3: oversaw the company’s expansion and helped steer J&J through the COVID‑19 vaccine rollout as CEO.

column1: Phebe Novakovic
column2: CEO of General Dynamics

column1: Novakovic previously worked in the U.S. government in roles at the Central Intelligence Agency and the Department of Defense before moving to the private sector in 2001. After working her way up at General Dynamics
column2: she now heads one of the Pentagon’s major defense contractors.

column1: Todd Combs
column2: Berkshire Hathaway investment manager

column1: Combs is a longtime Berkshire Hathaway investment manager and CEO of Geico who left Geico this week and is leaving his Berkshire role as well to lead JPMorgan Chase’s SRI Strategic Investment Group and join the advisory council in early 2026. For years
column2: he was one of Warren Buffett’s top stock pickers.

column1: Paul Ryan
column2: partner at Solamere Capital
column3: former Speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives

column1: Ryan is a partner at private equity firm Solamere Capital and formerly served as Speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives from 2015 to 2019
column2: where he was a key figure on fiscal and economic policy. He previously chaired both the House Budget Committee and the Ways and Means Committee
column3: making him a central Republican figure on fiscal and economic policy and tax legislation.

column1: National security experts
Condoleezza Rice
column2: former U.S. secretary of state

column1: Rice is a former U.S. secretary of state under George W. Bush from 2005 to 2009 and
column2: prior to that
column3: was national security adviser. She played a central role in U.S. foreign policy and national security decision-making in the 2000s.

column1: Robert Gates
column2: former U.S. secretary of defense

column1: Gates is a former CIA director under former President George H.W. Bush from 1991 to 1993 and former U.S. secretary of defense
column2: with a long career in national security and intelligence under both Republican and Democratic presidents.

column1: Chris Cavoli
column2: retired general

column1: Cavoli is a retired U.S. Army general who most recently served as Supreme Allied Commander Europe and Commander of U.S. European Command
column2: overseeing NATO forces and U.S. military operations in Europe.

column1: Ann Dunwoody
column2: retired commanding general of U.S. Army Materiel Command

column1: Dunwoody is a retired four‑star general and former commanding general of U.S. Army Materiel Command. She’s the first woman in U.S. history to achieve the rank of four‑star general.
Paul Nakasone
column2: retired general and former NSA director
